DAMGHANI:v1p146/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r4.claim: Ḥaml can mean pregnancy: the period ends when the pregnancy is delivered, and Mary became pregnant with Jesus.
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r4.anchor: الثامن : الحمل الحبل قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

BURSEVI:v5p249/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249/r1.claim: Trials burn away blameworthy dispositions, while patience produces divine and true qualities.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r1.anchor: بالبلاء تحترق الأوصاف الرديئة الخلقية وبالصبر يحصل الأخلاق الإلهية

BURSEVI:v5p249/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p249/r2.claim: Mary accepted Gabriel’s words; he came near, blew into her garment’s opening, and the breath reached her womb, so she conceived immediately.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فاطمأنت مريم إلى قول جبريل فدنا منها فنفخ

BURSEVI:v5p249/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249/r3.claim: Breath can reach the body without an opening; Adam’s spirit entered through the crown of his head and then spread through the body.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r3.anchor: وصول النفخ إلى الجوف لا يحتاج إلى منفذ من المنافذ كالفم ونحوه

BURSEVI:v5p249/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249/r4.claim: Jesus has bodily, spiritual, and unifying aspects: his body suggests Mary’s fluid, his reviving miracles suggest Gabriel’s breath, and their synthesis points to both.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r4.anchor: لعيسى عليه السلام جهة جسمانية وجهة روحانية وأحدية جمع للجهتين

BURSEVI:v5p249/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249/r5.claim: Bursevi says Gabriel’s human appearance caused Mary’s pleasure and fluid to enter the womb, so Jesus formed from her fluid; this rejects naturalists’ denial that one parent’s fluid alone can produce a child.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r5.anchor: فهو من ماء أمه فقط خلافا للطبيعيين فإنهم ينكرون وجود الولد من ماء أحد الزوجين

BURSEVI:v5p249/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249/r6.claim: The full human body came through Mary’s fluid and Gabriel’s human likeness preserved the usual human pattern; her imagining fluid made it occur, and the spirit’s endurance explains Jesus’ prolonged human form.
BURSEVI:v5p249/r6.anchor: وقد توهمت في النفخ الماء فحصل الماء المتوهم أيضا

BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r1.claim: Without Gabriel’s human likeness, Jesus would have appeared as a spirit; if Gabriel breathed while Mary was fearful, the child would inherit her harsh state.
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : لو لم يتمثل جبريل عند النفخ بالصورة البشرية

BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r2.claim: Stories say a mother’s sight at conception can shape a child, including snake-like and bear-like offspring, illustrating the transmission of parental states.
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r2.anchor: نقل في الأخبار : أن امرأة ولدت ولدا صورته صورة البشر وجسمه جسم الحية

BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r3.claim: Mary relaxed after hearing Gabriel was sent by God and recalled the angels’ good news; conception in that open-hearted state made Jesus open-hearted too.
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r3.anchor: فنفخ فيها في حين الانبساط والانشراح فخرج عيسى منبسطا منشرح الصدر

BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r4.claim: The account says Mary was thirteen and had menstruated twice before conception, and recommends that strong people imagine a well-formed man during intercourse.
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r4.anchor: قالوا : حملته وسنها وقتئذ ثلاث عشرة سنة وقد حاضت حيضتين قبل أن تحمل

BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the pregnancy and birth duration as one hour; some considered this strongest because Jesus was created directly, and the sequential fāʾ supports immediacy.
BURSEVI:v5p249#2/r5.anchor: ففي رواية عن ابن عباس كانت مدة الحمل والولادة ساعة واحدة

BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r1.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment or state: she withdrew while carrying Jesus in her womb; the distant place is construed as a destination reached by going.
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r1.anchor: فاعتزلت ملتبسة به أي : وهو في بطنها

BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r2.claim: Mary went from Jerusalem to a distant mountain or valley near Bethlehem, about six miles from Iliya.
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r2.anchor: مكاني دورز شهر ايليا كويند بكوهى رفت درجانب شرقي

BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r3.speaker: أنس
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r3.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s Isra account that Gabriel said he prayed at Bethlehem, where Jesus was born; Bursevi calls the report authentic or hasan and cites al-Nasa’i and al-Bayhaqi.
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r3.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث الإسراء

BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r4.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r4.claim: An alternative location is the far side of the house, which better fits the short pregnancy duration.
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r4.anchor: أو أقصى الدار وهو الأنسب لقصر مدة الحمل

BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r5.speaker: قصص الأنبياء
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r5.claim: As birth approached, Mary left Zakariya’s house at night for a place outside Jerusalem, wishing that Zakariya and others would not know.
BURSEVI:v5p250#2/r5.anchor: لما دنت ولادة مريم خرجت في حوف الليل من منزل زكريا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r1.claim: The explanatory fa implies that Mary trusted Gabriel; he approached and breathed into her garment, the breath entering her body and causing pregnancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r1.anchor: الفاء فصيحة أي فاطمأنت إلى قوله فدنا منها فنفخ في جيبها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the account that Gabriel approached and breathed into Mary's garment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r2.anchor: فدخلت النفخة في جوفها فحملته وروي هذا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r3.claim: Other accounts say Gabriel did not approach, but blew from a distance; further reports place the breath in her sleeve, hem, or mouth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r3.anchor: وقيل : لم يدن عليه السلام بل نفخ عن بعد فوصل الريح إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r4.claim: Reports differ on Mary's age: thirteen, fifteen from Wahb and Mujahid, fourteen, twelve, or ten; accounts also disagree whether she had menstruated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في سنها إذ ذاك فقيل ثلاث عشرة سنة وعن وهب ومجاهد خمس عشرة سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r5.claim: Views on gestation range from nine months, reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Baqir, to one hour, seven or six months, or eight months.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r5.anchor: ففي رواية عن ابن عباس أنها تسعة أشهر كما في سائر النساء وهو المروي عن الباقر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r6.claim: The instantaneous view cites the immediate sequence and 3:59's comparison with Adam; other reports name seven, six, or eight months.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r6.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه أنها كانت ساعة واحدة كما حملته ونبذته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r7.claim: Al-Alusi calls astrological explanations of survival by planetary months fables; naturalists give six months as the minimum.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r7.anchor: ومثل تلك الكلمات خرافات وكل امرأة تعرف أن النطفة إذا مضت عليها ثلاثة أشهر تتحرك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r8.claim: None of the contradictory reports is sound to him, but he inclines to the ordinary nine-month report and finds the instantaneous-birth argument inconclusive.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p79/r8.anchor: ولم يصح عندي شيء من هذه الأقوال المضطربة المتناقضة بيد أني أميل إلى أولها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r1.claim: Bāʾ in fan-tabadhat bihi means association: Mary withdrew while carrying him, with the phrase functioning as a circumstantial modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r1.anchor: فالباء للملابسة والمصاحبة مثلها في قوله تعالى ( تنبت بالدهن ) وقول المتنبي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r2.claim: The locative phrase describes her withdrawal to a remote place away from her family, behind a mountain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r2.anchor: بعيدا من أهلها وراء الجبل وأخرج عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد الزهد عن نوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r3.speaker: نوف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r3.claim: Nawf reports that after Gabriel's breath Mary conceived, felt labor pains as she grew heavy, and fled east in embarrassment; her people searched for her.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r3.anchor: عن نوف أن جبريل عليه السلام نفخ في جيبها فحملت حتى إذا أثقلت وجعت ما يجع النساء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r4.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r4.claim: Wahb's account says Joseph the carpenter, Mary's devoted cousin and fellow temple servant, questioned her pregnancy; she defended God's power with creation without seed or rain and Adam without parents.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r4.anchor: وروى الثعلبي في العرائس عن وهب قال : إن مريم لما حملت كان معها ابن عم لها يسمى يوسف النجار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r5.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r5.claim: In the same account, Joseph served for Mary during her weakness; near birth God told her to leave to protect her child, and Joseph carried her toward Egypt, where labor began.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r5.anchor: فلما دنا نفاسها أوحى الله تعالى إليها أن اخرجي من أرض قومك لئلا يقتلوا ولدك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r6.claim: Another report places Mary in the farthest room, which better fits the possibility that pregnancy lasted only briefly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p80/r6.anchor: وقيل : انتبذت أقصى الدار وهو الأنسب بقصر مدة الحمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r4.claim: One account says Gabriel lifted the front of her garment and blew into its collar, and she conceived when she put it on.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r4.anchor: {فحملته} قيل: إن جبريل رفع درعها فنفخ في جيبه (1) فحملت حين لبست.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r5.claim: Another account says Gabriel drew out the garment's collar with his finger and blew into it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r5.anchor: وقيل: مد جيب درعها بأصبعه ثم نفخ في الجيب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r6.claim: Other accounts place Gabriel's breath in her sleeve or mouth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r6.anchor: وقيل: نفخ في كم قميصها. وقيل: في فيها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r7.claim: Another account says Gabriel breathed from afar, and the wind reached her so she conceived Jesus immediately.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r7.anchor: وقيل: نفخ جبريل عليه السلام نفخا من بعيد فوصل الريح إليها فحملت بعيسى في الحال (2)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r8.claim: She withdrew and separated from her people while pregnant; qaṣiyyan means far away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r8.anchor: {فانتبذت به} أي تنحت بالحمل وانفردت، {مكانا قصيا} بعيدا من أهلها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r9.claim: The distant place was the far end of the valley, the Valley of Bethlehem; she fled so people would not shame her for bearing a child without a husband.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أقصى الوادي، وهو وادي بيت لحم، فرارا من قومها أن يعيروها بولادتها من غير زوج.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r10.claim: One view says her conception and delivery both occurred within an hour.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: كان الحمل والولادة في ساعة واحدة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r11.claim: One view gives her pregnancy the usual nine months.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r11.anchor: وقيل: كان مدة حملها تسعة أشهر كحمل سائر النساء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r12.claim: Another view gives eight months; Jesus' survival is presented as a sign because an eight-month infant was not thought to live.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r12.anchor: وقيل: كان مدة حملها ثمانية أشهر، وكان ذلك آية أخرى لأنه لا يعيش ولد يولد لثمانية أشهر، وولد عيسى لهذه المدة وعاش.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r13.claim: A further view gives her pregnancy six months.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r14.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r14.claim: Muqātil says conception, the child's formation, and birth happened within one hour at noon; Maryam was ten and had menstruated twice before conceiving.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p224/r14.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: حملته مريم في ساعة، وصور في ساعة، ووضعته في ساعة حين زالت الشمس

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r1.claim: Gabriel's breath entered Mary's garment and womb; reports give the gestation as seven, six, or eight months (the only surviving eight-month birth), or an instant. Mary was thirteen, or ten after two periods.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r1.anchor: بأن نفخ في درعها فدخلت النفخة في جوفها وكان مدة حملها سبعة أشهر

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r2.claim: Mary withdrew while carrying Jesus, as the cited poetic line illustrates the circumstantial attachment; she went beyond the mountain or to the far end of the house.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:22/r2.anchor: تدوس بنا الجماجم والتريبا والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال

QASHANI:19:22-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:22-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:22-24/r1.claim: Jesus's spirit connects with the semen only after it settles in the womb and unites into a temperament ready to receive the spirit.
QASHANI:19:22-24/r1.anchor: إنما يكون بعد حصول النطفة في الرحم واستقرارها فيه ريثما تمتزج وتتحد وتقبل مزاجا صالحا لقبول الروح

QASHANI:19:22-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:22-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:22-24/r2.claim: The phrase means Mary withdrew with the child, far from the eastern place, into the western natural and bodily horizon.
QASHANI:19:22-24/r2.anchor: أي: بعيدا من المكان الأول الشرقي لأنها وقعت به في المكان الغربي الذي هو عالم الطبيعة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r1.claim: Gabriel breathed through the opening of Mary's garment and the breath reached her womb, causing conception.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r1.anchor: فنفخ في درعها فوصل النفخ إلى جوفها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r2.claim: The sequential fa marks her immediate withdrawal with the child in her womb to a remote place, away from family or the eastern location.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r2.anchor: { فانتبذت به } أي فاعتزلت - وهو في بطنها - حالة { مكانا قصيا * }

DURR-FULL:v5p500/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p500/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p500/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary's distant place was far away.
DURR-FULL:v5p500/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {مكانا قصيا} قال نائيا

QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r15.claim: When Mary learned she was pregnant, she feared people's suspicion and had no trusted person to whom she could disclose the secret.
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r15.anchor: ولم تثق بأحد تفشي إليه سرها

QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r1.claim: Mary went to a distant place, and the pains of childbirth forced her to lean against a palm trunk.
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r1.anchor: مضت إلى مكان بعيد عن الخلق . ألجأها وجع الولادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r1.claim: The ف marks the consequence and close succession: Mary conceived immediately after the exchange; حملت means conception, while حملت به adds the sense of close attachment, illustrated by Abu Kabir al-Hudhali's poetry.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r2.claim: قصيا means far from her family; the word derives from distance and the passage gives no reason to specify a particular place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r2.anchor: و { قصيا } بعيدا ، أي بعيدا عن مكان أهلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r3.claim: An account that Mary fled to Egypt, helped by Yusuf the carpenter, and gave birth there is incorrect; Luke places the birth at Bethlehem in Judea, consistent with her later return to her people carrying Jesus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p84/r3.anchor: قيل : خرجت إلى البلاد المصرية فارة من قومها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.claim: Mary is said to have been thirteen years old when she conceived.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.anchor: ويذكر أنها كانت بنت ثلاث عشرة سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r10.claim: Fearing reproach and suspicion of wrongdoing, Mary withdrew far away in modesty and flight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r10.anchor: فلما أحست بذلك وخافت تعنيف الناس وأن يظن بها الشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r11.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r11.claim: One report says Mary fled to Egypt or a nearby region.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r11.anchor: روي في هذا أنها فرت إلى بلاد مصر أو نحوها قاله وهب بن منبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r12.claim: Another report places her at Bethlehem, four miles from Jerusalem (Iliya).
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p9#2/r12.anchor: وروي أيضا أنها خرجت إلى موضع يعرف (ببيت لحم) بينه وبين إيلياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r1.claim: The one Maryam conceived was Jesus.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r2.claim: One account says Gabriel breathed into the opening of her garment and the pregnancy took hold; al-Suddī says the breath entered her chest through the front slit and she conceived immediately.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r2.anchor: أن جبريل نفخ في جيب درعها فاستمر بها حملها رواه سعيد ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r3.claim: Another account says the one who spoke to Maryam was the one she carried, entering through her mouth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r3.anchor: الذي خاطبها هو الذي حملته ودخل من فيها قاله أبي بن كعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r4.claim: One report says she delivered as soon as she conceived, but Ibn al-Jawzi says this cannot mean literally at once because she withdrew while carrying him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r4.anchor: أنها حين حملت وضعت قاله ابن عباس والمعنى أنه ما طال حملها وليس المراد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r5.claim: He says the pregnancy lasted nine hours and she delivered that day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r5.anchor: أنها حملته تسع ساعات ووضعت من يومها قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r6.claim: They say Maryam carried Jesus for nine months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r6.anchor: تسعة أشهر قاله سعيد بن جير وابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r7.claim: He says the three-hour pregnancy comprised an hour to conceive, an hour to form, and an hour to deliver.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r7.anchor: ثلاث ساعات حملته في ساعة وصور في ساعة ووضعته في ساعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r8.claim: An eight-month pregnancy is proposed as a sign because no child born at eight months had survived.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r8.anchor: ثمانية أشهر فعاش ولم يعش مولود قط لثمانية أشهر فكان في هذا آية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r9.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r9.claim: One reported duration is six months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r9.anchor: والسادس في ستة اشهر حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r10.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r10.claim: Another report gives a duration of one hour.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r10.anchor: والسابع في ساعة واحدة حكاه الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r11.claim: They read qāṣiyan instead of qaṣiyyan; Isḥāq says she walked six miles, and al-Farrāʾ says both forms mean distant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة قاصيا قال ابن اسحاق مشت ستة أميال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r12.claim: She withdrew a distant way to escape her people's reproach for giving birth without a husband.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p218#2/r12.anchor: وإنما بعدت فرارا من قومها أن يعيروها بولادتها من غير زوج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r1.claim: Mary accepted God's decree; early scholars say Gabriel blew through her garment's opening, the breath reached her womb, and she conceived by God's permission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r1.anchor: فذكر غير واحد من علماء السلف أن الملك -وهو جبريل عليه السلام-عند ذلك نفخ في جيب درعها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r2.claim: Mary feared disbelief but confided in her sister, Zakariya's wife; both were pregnant and their family believed and trusted God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r2.anchor: غير أنها أفشت سرها وذكرت أمرها لأختها امرأة زكريا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r3.claim: Zakariya's wife's fetus prostrated to Mary's, meaning honor and humility; greeting prostration was lawful then but later forbidden to complete devotion to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r3.anchor: تجد الذي في جوفها (6) يسجد للذي في بطن مريم، أي: يعظمه ويخضع له،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r4.claim: Malik says Mary and Yahya's mother were cousins and conceived together; Yahya's mother felt her fetus prostrate to Mary's, which Malik attributes to Jesus' special status and miracles.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r4.anchor: قال مالك رحمه الله: بلغني أن عيسى ابن مريم ويحيى بن زكريا ابنا خالة، وكان حملهما جميعا معا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r5.claim: The majority say Mary's pregnancy lasted nine months.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r5.anchor: فالمشهور عن الجمهور أنها حملت به تسعة أشهر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r6.claim: Ikrima says the pregnancy lasted eight months, explaining that an eight-month infant does not live.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: ثمانية أشهر -قال: ولهذا لا يعيش ولد لثمانية أشهر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says conception and birth occurred without an interval; Ibn Kathir calls this strange and based on the verse's apparent sequence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p221#2/r7.anchor: سمع ابن عباس وسئل عن حبل مريم، قال: لم يكن إلا أن حملت فوضعت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r1.claim: The fāʾ marks succession but intervals depend on events: human development proceeds through stages, each forty days in sound reports, and rain makes earth green; Mary most likely carried Jesus the ordinary nine months.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r1.anchor: فالفاء وإن كانت للتعقيب، ولكن تعقيب (3) كل شيء بحسبه، كما قال تعالى: {ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r2.claim: Yusuf the carpenter, a righteous relative serving the sanctuary, noticed Mary's growing belly but reconsidered because he knew her purity; she answered his analogies by citing God's creation of trees, crops, and Adam without parents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r2.anchor: فلما رأى ثقل بطنها وكبره، أنكر ذلك من أمرها، ثم صرفه ما (5) يعلم من براءتها ونزاهتها ودينها وعبادتها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r3.claim: Mary withdrew when she sensed her people might suspect her, so they would neither see her nor be seen by her.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r3.anchor: ولما استشعرت مريم من قومها اتهامها بالريبة، انتبذت منهم مكانا قصيا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says pregnancy signs appeared after Mary drew water; people accused her and Yusuf because he was the only man with her in the church, so she hid behind a screen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p222/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: فلما حملت به وملأت قلتها (9) ورجعت، استمسك عنها الدم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Maryam felt reassured by the angel; he approached and blew into the opening of her garment, and the breath reached her womb, so she conceived.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فاطمأنت إلى قوله فدنا منها فنفخ في جيب درعها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r2.claim: Reported pregnancy durations include six months; seven months according to Ata, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Dahhak; eight months, with Jesus the only infant said to survive an eight-month birth; and three hours.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r2.anchor: وقيل : كانت مدة الحمل ستة أشهر . وعن عطاء وأبي العالية والضحاك : سبعة أشهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r3.claim: Another account says conception, formation, and birth each took an hour, with birth at midday; Ibn Abbas also reports a single hour from conception to birth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r3.anchor: وقيل : حملته في ساعة ، وصور في ساعة ، ووضعته في ساعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r4.claim: Reportedly Maryam conceived at age thirteen or ten and had menstruated twice before conceiving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r4.anchor: وقيل : حملته وهي بنت ثلاث عشرة سنة . وقيل : بنت عشر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r5.claim: People say every newborn cries at birth except Jesus.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r5.anchor: وقالوا : ما من مولود إلا يستهل غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r6.claim: Fantabadhat bihi means she withdrew while carrying him; the preposition makes a circumstantial phrase, as in the cited poem and 23:20, where the plant grows with its oil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r6.anchor: { فانتبذت به } أي اعتزلت وهو في بطنها ، كقوله : تدوس بنا الجماجم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r7.claim: Qaṣiyyan means far away from her people beyond the mountain, or at the far end of the house.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r7.anchor: { قصيا } بعيدا من أهلها وراء الجبل . وقيل : أقصى الدار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r8.speaker: السدي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r8.claim: One story says Maryam fled with her cousin Yusuf after people accused her of fornication; when he considered killing her, Gabriel told him the child was from the Holy Spirit, so he spared her.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p12/r8.anchor: وقيل : كانت سميت لابن عم لها اسمه يوسف ، فلما قيل : حملت من الزنا

FARRA:v2p162/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p162/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p162/r12.claim: Qaṣiyyan means remote, like qāṣiyan; an anonymous poem uses al-qaṣiyy to mean distant.
FARRA:v2p162/r12.anchor: وقوله: مكانا قصيا [22] (قاصيا) بمعنى واحد. أنشدني بعضهم.

FARRA:v2p162/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p162/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p162/r13.claim: An anonymous poem uses al-qaṣiyy for a distant place.
FARRA:v2p162/r13.anchor: لتقعدن مقعد القصي ... مني ذي القاذورة المقلي

MUJAHID:v1p385/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p385/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p385/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses a distant place as far off.
MUJAHID:v1p385/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ مكانا قصيا ﴾ قال يعني قاصيا

MUQATIL:19:22-23/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r1.claim: Mary was thirteen, bore Jesus in one hour, and he was formed and nursed in an hour at noon; she had menstruated twice before conceiving, lived with him thirty-three years, then six years after his ascension, and died aged fifty-two.
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r1.anchor: وهي ابنة ثلاث عشرة سنة، ومكثت مع عيسى، عليه السلام، ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

MUQATIL:19:22-23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r2.claim: Mary conceived, Jesus was formed, and she nursed him each within an hour at noon, after two menstrual periods.
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r2.anchor: فحملته أمه في ساعة واحدة، وصور في ساعة واحدة، وأرضعته في ساعة حين زالت الشمس من يومها

MUQATIL:19:22-23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r3.claim: Mary withdrew with Jesus to a distant place, away from her family beyond the hills.
MUQATIL:19:22-23/r3.anchor: يعني فانفردت بعيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم، { مكانا قصيا } [آية: 22]، يعني نائيا من أهلها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r1.claim: Mary was thirteen, ten, or twenty years old when she conceived.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r1.anchor: وكان سنها ثلاث عشرة سنه أو عشر أو عشرين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r2.claim: She withdrew while carrying Jesus in her womb, far from her family beyond a mountain, fearing blame when she realized she was pregnant.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r2.anchor: ﴿ فانتبذت به ﴾ اعتزلت وهو فى بطنها والجار والمجرور فى موضع الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gestation lasted one hour, and she delivered as soon as she conceived.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كانت مدة الحمل ساعه واحده كما حملته نبذته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r4.claim: Other reports give the pregnancy as six, seven, or eight months; one says no child born at eight months survived except Jesus.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r4.anchor: وقيل ستة أشهر وقيل سبعه وقيل ثمانيه ولم يعش مولود وضع لثمانيه إلا عيسى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r5.claim: Another report says she conceived and gave birth within an hour.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34/r5.anchor: وقيل حملته فى ساعة ووضعته في ساعة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r11.claim: Mary withdrew with the pregnancy to a distant place to avoid her people’s accusation that she had delivered without a husband.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r11.anchor: فرارا من تعيير قومها إياها بالولادة من غير زوج

QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas locates the distant place at the far end of the Wadi of Bethlehem, four miles from Jerusalem.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r12.anchor: إلى أقصى الوادي، وهو وادي بيت لحم بينه وبين إيلياء أربعة أميال

QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says conception was followed immediately by birth; Qurtubi calls this the more apparent reading because withdrawal follows conception in the account.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:19-23/r13.anchor: ما هو إلا أن حملت فوضعت في الحال وهذا هو الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.claim: The Quran describes God's breathing into Mary and into Adam; Razi notes that the wording concerning Jesus can grammatically refer to Mary because Jesus was in her womb.

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r2.claim: One group says God Himself was the breather, citing the wording about breathing His spirit into Jesus and the analogy to Adam.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم كان النفخ من الله تعالى لقوله

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r3.claim: Others say Gabriel breathed, since “I shall grant you” suggests the pregnancy was caused through his action by God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : النافخ هو جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r4.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r4.claim: Wahb's account has Gabriel blow into Mary's collar, with the breath reaching her womb.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r4.anchor: قول وهب إنه نفخ جبريل في جيبها حتى وصلت إلى الرحم

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r5.claim: Another account places Gabriel's breath in the lower hem, from which it reached the womb.

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r6.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Gabriel blew through the sleeve into Mary's chest; Zachariah's wife realized she was pregnant when embracing her and said the child in her womb bowed to Mary's child.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r6.anchor: قول السدي أخذ بكمها فنفخ في جنب درعها فدخلت النفخة صدرها

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r7.claim: A further view says the breath entered Mary's mouth, reached her belly, and she conceived immediately.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r7.anchor: أن النفخة كانت في فيها فوصلت إلى بطنها فحملت في الحال

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r8.claim: The narrative has an omitted clause: the matter was decreed, Gabriel breathed into Mary, and she conceived.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r8.anchor: إذ عرفت هذا ظهر أن في الكلام حذفا وهو

RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r9.claim: Reports put Mary's age at conception at thirteen or twenty and say she had menstruated twice, but the Quran establishes none of these details.
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r9.anchor: قيل حملته وهي بنت ثلاث عشرة سنة

RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r1.claim: “She withdrew with him” means she withdrew while Jesus was inside her, like a plant that grows bearing oil within it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r1.anchor: أي اعتزلت وهو في بطنها كقوله

RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r6.claim: Other proposed reasons for Mary's withdrawal are embarrassment before Zachariah, shame given her reputation for piety, or fear for the child's safety; Razi says the text chooses none.
RAZI-FULL:v21p172/r6.anchor: استحيت من زكريا فذهبت إلى مكان بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r8.claim: The “Be, and it is” analogy with Adam in Āl ʿImrān also supports instantaneous conception, since a gestational interval applies to conception from semen.
RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r8.anchor: فثبت أن عيسى عليه السلام كما قال الله تعالى له

RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p172#2/r9.claim: Qaṣiy means distant; some locate the place at the farthest edge of the home, behind a mountain, or on the journey with her cousin Yusuf.

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r89.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r89.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r89.claim: Mary conceives when the Spirit is breathed into her; a common account says it was through her shirt opening or sleeve.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r89.anchor: according to a common account, the Spirit was breathed through the opening of her shirt or its sleeve

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r90.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r90.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r90.claim: Jesus’ divine-fiat creation resembles Adam’s being given life by God’s breath, while 3:59 explicitly grounds their likeness in divine creation.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r90.anchor: Adam is similarly brought to life when God breathed into him of His Spirit

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r91.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r91.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r91.claim: A report says Zachariah’s pregnant wife met Mary and the child John prostrated in the womb toward Jesus, fulfilling John’s role as confirmer.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r91.anchor: the child in the womb of Zachariah’s wife seemed to prostrate before the child in Mary’s

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r92.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r92.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r92.claim: Some identify the distant place with the eastern area near the Temple, but the author finds more convincing a remote place where Mary was unknown.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r92.anchor: However, others describe it more convincingly as a distant place where she and her family were not known

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r93.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r93.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r93.claim: Mary went far away to spare Zachariah embarrassment and protect herself and the child from people who might misunderstand her piety.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r93.anchor: She goes far off in order to avoid embarrassing Zachariah as well as out of fear for her child

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r94.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r94.speaker: Wahb ibn Munabbih
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r94.claim: Wahb reports that Mary’s relative Joseph, who served in the Temple, knew of the pregnancy and helped her.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r94.anchor: Wahb ibn Munabbih, who was familiar with the Jewish and Christian scriptures, reports that Mary’s pregnancy was known to one of her relatives named Joseph

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r95.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r95.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r95.claim: Some accounts say Mary and Joseph later fled to Egypt as delivery approached.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r95.anchor: Some accounts assert that she later fled with Joseph to Egypt as her time of delivery drew near

NAHHAS:v3p9/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p9/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p9/r10.claim: قصيا is locative; alternatively it is an object, meaning she withdrew with him to a distant place.
NAHHAS:v3p9/r10.anchor: ظرف وإن شئت كان مفعولا أي فقصدت به مكانا

TAB-FULL:v15p490/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r1.claim: Wahb says Gabriel appeared as a man, breathed through the opening of Mary's garment, and the breath reached her womb, causing conception.
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r1.anchor: قال: سمعت وهبا، قال: لما أرسل الله جبريل إلى مريم تمثل لها بشرا سويا فقالت له:

TAB-FULL:v15p490/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r2.claim: In another report, Mary submitted to God's command; Gabriel breathed into her garment neckline and left.
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r2.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه اليماني، قال: لما قال ذلك، يعني لما قال جبريل {قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين} [مريم: 9] . . الآية استسلمت لأمر الله،

TAB-FULL:v15p490/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Gabriel held Mary's sleeves, breathed into her split neckline, and the breath entered her chest; her pregnant sister later said John's fetus prostrated to Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: طرحت عليها جلبابها لما قال جبريل ذلك لها، فأخذ جبريل بكميها، فنفخ في جيب درعها

TAB-FULL:v15p490/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the saying that Gabriel breathed into the neckline and sleeve of Mary's garment.
TAB-FULL:v15p490/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج: يقولون: إنه إنما نفخ في جيب درعها وكمها

TAB-FULL:v15p491/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r1.claim: Mary withdrew with Jesus to a remote place; qasiyy means far away, from the verb for becoming distant or removing something.
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r1.anchor: يقول: فاعتزلت بالذي حملته، وهو عيسى، وتنحت به عن الناس {مكانا قصيا} [مريم: 22] يقول: مكانا نائيا قاصيا عن الناس،

TAB-FULL:v15p491/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r2.claim: A rajaz line uses al-qasiyy for someone seated far away, supporting the meaning of remoteness.
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r2.anchor: لتقعدن مقعد القصي … مني ذي القاذورة المقلي

TAB-FULL:v15p491/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the place remote, and Mujahid says it is distant.
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا} [مريم: 22] قال: مكانا نائيا

TAB-FULL:v15p491/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Mary went to the far eastern side of the sanctuary as delivery approached.
TAB-FULL:v15p491/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: لما بلغ أن تضع، مريم، خرجت إلى جانب المحراب الشرقي منه فأتت أقصاه

TAB-FULL:v15p495/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r1.claim: Wahb recounts that Mary and her relative Joseph the carpenter served the temple near Mount Zion; Joseph noticed her pregnancy and struggled between suspicion and her known virtue before accepting God's power to create without ordinary means.
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r1.anchor: قال: ثني عبد الصمد بن معقل، أنه سمع وهب بن منبه، يقول: لما اشتملت مريم على الحمل، كان معها قرابة لها، يقال له يوسف النجار،

TAB-FULL:v15p495/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r2.claim: Joseph took over Mary's temple work as her strength failed; God told her to leave her people lest they shame her and kill the child.
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r2.anchor: فلما دنا نفاسها أوحى الله إليها أن اخرجي من أرض قومك، فإنهم إن ظفروا بك عيروك، وقتلوا ولدك،

TAB-FULL:v15p495/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r3.claim: Mary told her pregnant sister, the mother of John; when they met, the child in the sister's womb prostrated in recognition of Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v15p495/r3.anchor: فلما التقيا وجدت أم يحيى ما في بطنها خر لوجهه ساجدا معترفا لعيسى،

TABATABAI:19:21-24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r4.claim: Qasiy means far away: Mary conceived and withdrew with the child to a distant place apart from her people.
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r4.anchor: القصي البعيد أي حملت بالولد فانفردت

TABATABAI:19:40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:40/r3.speaker: الإمام الباقر
TABATABAI:19:40/r3.claim: A report says Gabriel blew into Mary’s garment and the child was completed in her womb immediately, just as a normal pregnancy takes nine months.
TABATABAI:19:40/r3.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام أنه يعني جبرئيل تناول جيب مدرعتها فنفخ فيه نفخة فكمل الولد في الرحم

TABATABAI:19:40/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:40/r4.speaker: الإمام الصادق
TABATABAI:19:40/r4.claim: Another report gives Mary’s pregnancy as nine hours; other narrations say six months.
TABATABAI:19:40/r4.anchor: وهذا مروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:19:40/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:40/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:40/r5.claim: The author notes some narrations giving the pregnancy as six months.
TABATABAI:19:40/r5.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أن مدة حملها كانت ستة أشهر

TABRISI:19:21-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:21-30/r3.claim: Qasiy means far away, as opposed to near.

TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r3.claim: Mary conceived Jesus and withdrew to a distant place, away from relatives through shame and fear of accusation.
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r3.anchor: أي تنحت الحمل إلى مكان بعيد

TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r4.claim: One report says Gabriel took the edge of Mary’s garment and blew into it, and she conceived immediately.
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r4.anchor: إن جبرائيل أخذ ردن قميصها بإصبعه فنفخ فيه

TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r5.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r5.claim: Another report says Gabriel blew into the neckline; the fetus completed instantly, Mary felt the weight, and she left ashamed after her aunt failed to recognize her.
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r5.anchor: تناول جيب مدرعتها فنفخ فيه نفخة فكمل الولد في الرحم

TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r6.claim: The interval from Mary’s withdrawal to conception was only an hour, inferred from the immediate sequence of the verbs.
TABRISI:19:21-30#2/r6.anchor: لم يكن بين الانتباذ والحمل إلا ساعة واحدة

THALABI:v6p210/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p210/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p210/r2.claim: The reported duration of Mary's pregnancy varies: nine months, eight months with Jesus uniquely surviving an eight-month birth, six months, three hours, or one hour.
THALABI:v6p210/r2.anchor: واختلفوا في مدة حملها ووقت وضعها، فقال بعضهم: كان مقدار حملها تسعة أشهر كحمل سائر النساء،

THALABI:v6p210/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p210/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p210/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says she conceived and gave birth immediately, with only an hour between pregnancy and withdrawing, since the Quran names no interval.
THALABI:v6p210/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما هو إلا أن حملت فوضعت ولم يكن بين الحمل والانتباذ إلا ساعة:

THALABI:v6p210/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p210/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
THALABI:v6p210/r4.claim: Muqatil says Mary conceived, the child formed, and she gave birth in successive hours at noon; she was ten and had menstruated twice before conceiving.
THALABI:v6p210/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: حملته مريم في ساعة وصور في ساعة ووضعته في ساعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r1.claim: The wording is abridged: Gabriel breathed into Maryam, and the omitted event is clear from other passages because the Quran is one book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r1.anchor: - قوله تعالى: {فحملته} هو مختصر والمعنى: فنفخ فيها جبريل فحملته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r2.claim: Gabriel approached, took the edge of her garment, and breathed into it; she conceived Jesus immediately and felt the pregnancy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r2.anchor: فنفخ فيه فحملت مريم من ساعتها بعيسى ووجدت حس الحمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r3.claim: The remote place was the far end of a valley, identified as the valley of Bethlehem.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r4.claim: Maryam withdrew with the pregnancy to a distant place, later at delivery, to avoid reproach from Zechariah and her people for giving birth without a husband.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r4.anchor: إنما كان عند وضعها، فرارا من زكريا ومن قومها أن يعيروها بولادتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r5.claim: He says conception was followed by birth without an extended interval; the author reads the sequence as indicating withdrawal at delivery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r5.anchor: ما هو إلا أن حملت فوضعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r6.claim: Al-qasiy means one who is distant, derived from the verb for being far; a cited rajaz line witnesses the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p217/r6.anchor: والقصي فعيل بمعنى فاعل من قصى يقصو إذا بعد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:19-22/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:19-22/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:19-22/r5.claim: Mary withdrew far away to the far end of the Wadi of Bethlehem after sensing pregnancy, fleeing her people for fear of blame.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:19-22/r5.anchor: فحملته فانتبذت به } تباعدت بالحمل { مكانا قصيا } بعيدا من أهلها في أقصى وادي بيت لحم، وذلك أنها لما أحست بالحمل، هربت من قومها مخافة اللائمة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r9.claim: Gabriel took Mary's garment opening with his finger and blew into it; the breath reached her womb and she conceived.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r9.anchor: فأخذ جبريل جيبها بأصبعه فنفخ فيه، فصار إلى بطنها فحملت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r10.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Mary carried Jesus for nine months.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r10.anchor: قال: {فحملته} [مريم: 22] قال الحسن: تسعة أشهر في بطنها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r11.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r11.claim: Qatāda explains Mary's withdrawal with Jesus as her going off to a distant, secluded place.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p219/r11.anchor: قوله: {فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا} [مريم: 22] سعيد، عن قتادة قال: أي فانفردت به مكانا شاسعا منتحيا.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r1.claim: Mary conceived when God caused the spirit to be breathed through an angel, as also stated in 21:91 and 66:12.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r1.anchor: Allah melek vasıtasıyla ruhu üfleyince Meryem hamile kaldı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r2.claim: Commentaries report gestation periods ranging from one hour to nine months; Ibn Kathir says most held it was nine months.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r2.anchor: Tefsirlerde hamilelikle ilgili olarak bir saat ile dokuz ay arasında farklı sürelerden söz edilmiş olmakla birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r3.claim: Mary withdrew to a distant place and concealed the pregnancy for a time because she feared people's reproach.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:22/r3.anchor: insanların kendisini kınayacağından endişe ettiği için, durumu ailesinden gizlemek maksadıyla uzak bir yere çekilerek bir müddet hamileliğini gizledi

SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r1.claim: In fa-intabadhat bihi, the prepositional phrase is circumstantial: she withdrew while carrying him with her.
SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r1.anchor: قوله: { فانتبذت به }: الجار والمجرور في محل نصب على الحال، أي: انتبذت وهو مصاحب لها

SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:22/r2.claim: An unattributed poetic line with banā illustrates the accompaniment sense.

ZAJJAJ:v3p323/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p323/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p323/r4.claim: Intabadhat bihi means she went away with the child, and qaṣiyyan or qāṣiyyan both mean distant.
ZAJJAJ:v3p323/r4.anchor:
(انتبذت به) تباعدت به.
وقصيا وقاصيا في معنى واحد،

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#4/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the distant place as a remote place.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا ﴾ قال متنحيا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that Mary did no more than conceive and then give birth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r4.anchor: عن رجل عمن سمع ابن عباس يقول في مريم يقول ليس إلا أن حملته ثم وضعت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r11.claim: Reports give Mary's age as fourteen or fifteen years, the latter attributed to Wahb and Mujāhid, or thirteen, twelve, or ten.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r11.anchor: قيل: وكانت بنت أربع عشرة سنة. وقيل: بنت خمس عشرة سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r12.claim: Reports conflict on whether Mary had menstruated: some say after two periods, some say she had not yet menstruated, and others say she never menstruated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r12.anchor:
قيل:
بعد أن حاضت حيضتين. وحكى محمد بن الهيصم أنها لم تكن حاضت بعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r13.claim: Some say Mary fled to Egypt; others locate the birth near Bethlehem, behind a mountain, or at the farthest part of her house.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r13.anchor: روي أنها فرت إلى بلاد مصر أو نحوها قاله وهب. وقيل: إلى موضع يعرف ببيت لحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r14.claim: Mary withdrew a great distance in shame and fear that people would suspect her of wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p249/r14.anchor: فلما أحست وخافت ملامة الناس أن يظن بها الشر فارتمت به إلى مكان قصي حياء وفرارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r1.claim: One story says Mary was betrothed to her cousin Yusuf; after a pregnancy rumor, he fled with her, then nearly killed her until Gabriel told him the child was from the Holy Spirit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r1.anchor: وقيل: كانت سميت لابن عم لها اسمه يوسف فلما قيل حملت من الزنا خاف عليها قتل الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r2.claim: Some reports say the pregnancy lasted three hours, with conception, formation, and birth taking one hour each.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r2.anchor:
وقيل: كانت مدة الحمل ثلاث ساعات. وقيل:
حمل في ساعة وصور في ساعة ووضعته في ساعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r3.speaker: عطاء وأبو العالية والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk give a seven-month pregnancy; other reports say six or eight months.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r3.anchor: وعن عطاء وأبي العالية والضحاك: سبعة أشهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r4.claim: The author calls the pregnancy-duration reports contradictory and says commentators should have left them aside.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p250/r4.anchor: وهذه أقوال مضطربة متناقضة كان ينبغي أن يضرب عنها صفحا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.claim: The repeated فاء marks succession, with each event following according to its natural interval; it does not require every sequence to be instantaneous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.anchor: تكرر استخدام حرف الفاء وهي تفيد تعقيب كل شيء بحسبه أي تفيد تعقيب الأحداث التي وردت في السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r2.claim: Mary conceived after the spirit was breathed into her, withdrew, and carried the pregnancy for its customary term without an intervening obstacle, explaining the sequence of فاء clauses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r2.anchor: فمريم عليها السلام حملت عندما نفخ فيها ثم لم يكن هناك أي معوقات بعدها فانتبذت مكاناً قصياً

BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r1.speaker: محمد رسول الله
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r1.claim: In the letter to the Negus, Jesus is called God's spirit and word cast to the pure virgin Mary, and his conception is compared with Adam's creation by God's hand and breath.
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r1.anchor: من محمد رسول الله إلى النجاشي ملك الحبشة سلم أنت فإني أحمد إليك الله الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن وأشهد أن عيسى ابن مريم روح الله

BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r2.speaker: محمد رسول الله
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r2.claim: The letter invites the Negus and his troops to worship God alone, obey and follow Muhammad, and believe in his revelation; it closes by affirming that the message was delivered sincerely.
BAQILLANI:v1p134#2/r2.anchor: وإني أدعوك إلى الله وحده لا شريك له والموالاة على طاعته وأن تتبعني وتؤمن بالذي جاءني
